tools.name: describe_ui
tools.description: The app facts the app plugin reports for the live client: activeTab, the navigate targets (navTargets: the friendly names, and navTargetEntryPointIds: the entry-point ids), the toolbar's toolbarActions (id/label/enabled/submenu), the menu bar's leaf menuPaths, navEntryPoints (roots, children), the open view's viewTabs and sections (every section it registered, including one never built - 'created':false; target it by its 'id') with sectionProblems, and any waiting dialog ('dialog': title, message, buttons - answer it with the 'answer' verb). Tables, buttons and fields are read from the element tree with 'snapshot' or 'read'. Pass 'fields' to get only the parts you need.

fields.description: Only these top-level fields, e.g. ["sections","dialog"] or ["activeTab","viewTabs"]; default all.

tools.name: do_action
tools.description: Execute ONE flow step against the live client and return pass/fail and its duration ('ms'). A step is a verb (click, type, press, ..., contextMenu) or one of the app steps navigate, close, loginAs. A successful step with a Java form is recorded for export_test; one without (a loginAs after the first step, a target by ref) runs but is not recorded, and 'notRecorded' says why. The 'action' object uses the flow schema, e.g. {"action":"navigate","target":"home"} or {"action":"expect","target":{"role":"table"},"rows":{"op":"gte","value":1}}. A step that opens a message or confirmation returns at once with 'dialog' (title, message, buttons); navigate, close and loginAs refuse to run until it is answered with the 'answer' verb.

action.description: A flow step named by its 'action' field: a verb, or navigate / close / loginAs. The verbs are also tools of their own, with full argument schemas.

record.description: false keeps this step out of export_test's recording (used by tests)

_lease.description: lease token from session op 'lease'; omit while nobody holds the lease

tools.name: do_actions
tools.description: Execute SEVERAL flow steps in order against the live client, in one call, stopping at the first failure. Prefer this over repeated do_action when the next steps are already known. Returns {passed, ran, total, steps:[{passed, action, message}]}; successful steps are recorded for export_test exactly as do_action records them. Example: {"actions":[{"action":"navigate","target":"home"},{"action":"click","target":{"role":"tab","name":"Customer"}},{"action":"close"}]}.

actions.description: Flow actions to run in order

items.description: A flow step named by its 'action' field: a verb, or navigate / close / loginAs. The verbs are also tools of their own, with full argument schemas.

_lease.description: lease token from session op 'lease'; omit while nobody holds the lease

tools.name: batch
tools.description: Run SEVERAL steps in ONE call, in order, stopping at the first that does not pass - use it whenever the next steps are already known. Each step runs, answers and records exactly as its own tool call would, so export_test writes the same test either way; 'read' steps record nothing, and a 'read' that finds nothing stops the batch. Returns {passed, ran, total, ms, steps:[{verb, passed, message, ms, recorded?, notRecorded?, ...}], snapshot?}. A harness error (CAPABILITY_GAP, INPUT_ERROR) is a tool error naming the step; the steps before it ran and were recorded. Example: {"steps":[{"verb":"click","target":{"role":"tab","name":"Customer"}},{"verb":"type","target":{"role":"text","name":"Name"},"text":"X"},{"verb":"expect","target":{"role":"button","name":"Save"},"state":["!disabled"]}]}.

steps.description: The steps, in order. Each is {"verb": <name>, ...the arguments that verb's own tool takes}.

verb.description: A verb tool's name (click, type, press, check, select, pick, menu, context_menu, answer, choose_file, drag, drop, expect, scroll, set_clipboard), 'read', or a flow step type (navigate, close, loginAs, screenshot, ...).

snapshot.description: true, or the snapshot tool's arguments (target, depth, compact, ...): a snapshot taken after the last step that ran, pass or fail.

_lease.description: lease token from session op 'lease'; omit while nobody holds the lease

tools.name: export_test
tools.description: Write the steps recorded since the last session reset as a JUnit @UiTest class under <module>/src/test/java/<package>/<class>.java (the module is the app plugin's export module, else the working directory; -Dswingui.testsDir overrides). The test starts where the recording did, right after a reset, so it must begin by getting to its own starting screen: without an app plugin a reset only closes dialogs, and startWarning flags a test that does not begin with menu, press or navigate. Only steps with a Java form are recorded (verbs, including expect for checks; navigate, close, a leading loginAs). Refuses a recording that did not begin at a reset, a bad class/method/package name, an existing file, or an empty recording, naming each problem; a refusal keeps the recording.

class.description: Test class name; must end in UiIT, e.g. OrderSaveUiIT

package.description: Java package (default: the app plugin's export package, else 'recorded')

clear.description: Empty the recording after exporting (default: true); reset before recording the next test

_lease.description: lease token from session op 'lease'; omit while nobody holds the lease

tools.name: snapshot
tools.description: The live client as an element tree: every showing window, dialog and popup (focused window first, popups last), each element with role, name, value, state and a ref (e1, e2, ...). Refs stay valid until the next snapshot; pass one as {"ref":"e12"} as a verb's target. SCOPE IT: an unscoped snapshot is the whole app and costs thousands of tokens. Give a 'target' locator (e.g. {"scope":["tab:Customer"],"role":"section","name":"Header"} or {"role":"tab","name":"Line items"}) for one element's subtree, 'depth' for a few levels, and compact:true to drop rows and items. The answer ends with 'size' {nodes, bytes, scoped}.

window.description: Only the roots this names: main | popup | dialog | dialog:<title> | window:<title>

ref.description: Only this element's subtree (a ref from the previous snapshot)

target.description: Only this element's subtree, found like a verb's target - a tab's content for a tab. At most one of window, ref and target.

ref.description: Ref from the last snapshot, e.g. e12; valid until the next snapshot.

window.description: main | popup | dialog | dialog:<title> | window:<title>; a title ending in * matches a prefix.

scope.description: Ordered tab:<title> / section:<caption> steps the element sits in (a section is any titled border, even one on a clickable box); an id:<name> step means strictly inside the component whose getName() is <name> (not a contributed section id).

name.description: Its name: component name, own text, label, titled border, tooltip, or action name.

row.description: Table row: {"<column header>": "<cell text>", ...} or {"index": n}.

column.description: Table column header: with row, that cell; without row, the header itself.

item.description: List or combo item text (one element), or a tree path.

point.description: {x, y}: fractions (0..1) of the element's bounds, for custom-painted content.

nth.description: Which match, in tree order, when the locator is not unique (makes the step fragile).

depth.description: Levels of nodes to include below the windows (or the scoped element), which is level 1; deeper nodes are cut and their parent marked truncated. 2-4 is usually enough.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: A PNG of the app: the target element, or the current window when no target is given. It PAINTS the app's own components into an offscreen image - it never grabs the screen - so it captures the client whether or not it is in front, takes no focus, and cannot catch another application's window. Give a 'target' for one dialog, panel, table or toolbar, and 'region' for a snippet inside it. Anything drawn in a window of its own (an open popup menu, a combo dropdown, a tooltip) is NOT in the image - capture that window instead. A read: nothing is recorded and there is no flow step for it. Use it for an aesthetic call - alignment, cropping, overlap, proportion - and an 'expect' for anything that is really a number or a boolean.

tools.name: inspect
tools.description: Work WITH the person at the app (only when it was started with inspector=on; otherwise a CAPABILITY_GAP). highlight: box every match of 'target' (numbered when several) with 'question' on a bar; they click the check mark on the one they mean (outcome confirmed, chosen n, its locator) or 'None of these' (rejected). pick: they click the element they mean - the click does not reach the app - and you get its locator. recording: what the person recorded. THEY start it with ● Record in the palette in the app window and end it with Done - every step they take is recorded as if you had run it, Check mode adds checks, Steps replays, redoes or deletes - you only read it (outcome idle, recording or done; 'wait' waits for their Done) and export it with export_test. steps: the recording so far. hover: a box follows their pointer and names the locator under it. clear: removes your boxes and question. While a person records, picks, answers or replays, no test run can take the lease.

The tokens: disabled, focused, selected, checked, readonly, editable, rollover, editing (a table with an open cell editor), atTop and atBottom (a scrollable element's viewport), expanded and leaf (a tree row), and any state the app reports for a section (e.g. hidden, incomplete). tools.name: scroll
tools.description: Scrolls a table, tree, list or panel: to an end with 'to', by whole screens with 'pages', or until a row is in view by giving the target a 'row'. Exactly one of the three. It moves the viewport directly rather than posting wheel input, so it is exact and it fires the same change a scroll bar does - which is what continuous paging listens for. Read where it ended up from the element's 'scroll' block (x, y, width, height, maxX, maxY) or its atTop/atBottom states. Returns {passed, reason?, message, ms, recorded, pending?, realInput?, activations?, snapshot?}; the recorded step is what export_test writes (a ref becomes a locator; via:api marks a direct Swing call, fragile:true a target that needed nth).

target.description: The scrollable element; add a 'row' to it to scroll that row into view.

tools.name: set_clipboard
tools.description: Puts text on the system clipboard, as a copy in another application would - e.g. a block copied from Excel: a tab between cells, a line break between rows, each value as displayed. Paste it into the app with press "Mod+V" on the focused element (click the anchor cell first). It REPLACES what the user had on the clipboard. Read it back with read_clipboard. tools.name: session
tools.description: The agent itself. info (default): versions, app start, lease, plugins (the plugins array lists every plugin with its state). lease {owner, ttlMs}: take the agent for one owner; pass the token as _lease on every mutating call. release {token}. renew {token}: keep the lease alive while the test makes no call; answers renewed: false once the lease is gone. reset {alias | user+password}: the start of every test: close modal dialogs; with an app plugin also its reset (tabs, login as alias or user). Starts a fresh recording for export_test. login {alias | user+password | relogin:true}: switch users mid-test. edt: the client's event-thread stack.
